rules.value_as_published: October 19 is the last day you can register to vote online for the November 3, 2026 General Election; mail applications must be postmarked 14 days before Election Day or sooner. (State calendar: Monday, Oct. 19, 2026, deadline to register by mail or online, MCL 168.497.)

Registration is available in person through 8 p.m. on Election Day; within 14 days of the election (from Tuesday, Oct. 20, 2026) registration must be done in person with the local clerk with proof of residency.

Detroit City Clerk's Office, 2 Woodward Ave #200, Detroit, MI 48226, Monday through Friday 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., (313) 224-3270; Department of Elections, 2978 W. Grand Blvd., same hours. On Election Day, unregistered voters can register and vote at the Department of Elections (2978 W. Grand Blvd) and the Detroit City Clerk's Office (2 Woodward Ave).

Within 14 days of the election or on Election Day, one proof of residency: Michigan driver's license or state ID card; utility bill, bank statement, paycheck, or government check with name and Detroit address; any other government document with your name and Detroit address.
Michigan Online Voter Registration System (personal lookup; link-out only).

Request online (Michigan Voter Information Center), call the Detroit City Clerk at (313) 224-3270 to have an application mailed, or download the State application form and mail it to Detroit City Clerk, 2 Woodward Ave #200, Detroit, MI 48226.
We recommend that you request your absentee ballot for the November 3, 2026 General Election by October 13th.
Online applications may be submitted until 5 p.m. the Friday before Election Day (Oct. 30, 2026); plan on submitting at least 15 days before Election Day.

Monday, Nov. 2, 2026, 4 p.m.: deadline for a registered voter to apply for an AV ballot in person at the clerk's office (MCL 168.759). Election Day registrants may obtain and vote an absent voter ballot in person in the clerk's office on Nov. 3, 2026.

Absent voter ballots must be available for issuance to voters Thursday, Sept. 24, 2026. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, you can vote early in person with an absentee ballot at the Detroit City Clerk's office starting on September 24, until November 2 at 4 p.m. if registered at your current address.

Your ballot must be received by the Detroit City Clerk by 8 p.m. on Election Day. Military and overseas voters: postmarked by Election Day and received within 6 days after (State: by Monday, Nov. 9, 2026).
Recommended mail-back date October 20 for most voters.

Mail (signed envelope required); any Detroit drop box or Early Voting Site; delivery by a family or household member; or request pickup by calling (313) 224-3270 before 5 p.m. the last Friday before Election Day.
Track absentee ballot status at the Michigan Voter Information Center (personal lookup; link-out only).
Voters may opt in to the permanent mail ballot list to automatically receive ballots for all future elections.

For the November General Election, Detroit Early Vote Sites are open daily from October 24 to November 2 from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. (State: mandatory early voting Saturday, Oct. 24 through Sunday, Nov. 1, 2026; optionally the Monday before Election Day until 4 p.m.)

When you vote at an Early Voting Site, your voting experience will be similar to that of voting at a polling place on Election Day. You will complete your ballot, place it in a secrecy sleeve, and then deposit it into the voting tabulator.
Polls are open from 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. If you are in line by 8 p.m. at your polling place, you will be able to vote.

Voters present one form of proof: Michigan driver's license or state ID; utility bill, bank statement, paycheck, or government check with name and Detroit address; any other government document with name and Detroit address. (State law: a voter without photo ID may sign an affidavit and vote a regular ballot; confirm on the SOS voter page.)
Find your polling place at the Michigan Voter Information Center (personal lookup; link-out only). In-app: point-in-polygon on the City precinct layer.
Detroit City Clerk, (313) 224-3270, 2 Woodward Ave #200, Detroit, MI 48226, cityclerkhelpdesk@detroitmi.gov. Election Protection Hotline (866) 687-8683.

detroitmi.gov/departments/elections served a Cloudflare bot challenge to this connector on 2026-09-21; it was not bypassed. Rules above come from detroitvotes.org (the Department's public voter site) and the Michigan Secretary of State.
